title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Fix a genus g (g ≥ 2 if needed). Fix a rigidifying functor for curves, i.e. an auxiliary level structure such as a Jacobi structure of suitable level; this is Grothendieck's device from his 1960-61 Cartan seminar. With it the moduli of smooth, proper, geometrically connected genus-g curves is representable, a 'multiplicité modulaire' M_g, and one can work over that base.

The new moduli problem. M_g^𝔖(S) is the set of pairs (X/S, P), where:
- X/S is a relative curve of genus g;
- P → X is a P^1-bundle, i.e. a torsor under GP(1) = PGL_2;
- P carries an '𝔖-structure' relative to S, meaning an integrable (flat) connection or stratification relative to S.

This is the relative de Rham moduli of flat PGL_2-bundles over M_g. Its fibre over [X] is the PGL_2 de Rham moduli of X, analytically the PGL_2 character variety. In the context of 'Connexions projectives et uniformisation', the projective structures (uniformizing opers) sit inside this space.

To get a good moduli problem he imposes a non-degeneracy condition at every geometric point s: P_s must not reduce, compatibly with the connection, to G_m ⊂ PGL_2 or to G_a ⊂ PGL_2. He calls such P 'irreducible' and says this avoids the degenerate cases.

Proposition. Let X be a connected algebraic scheme over an algebraically closed field k, and P a P^1-bundle on X with 𝔖-structure. He asserts the following are equivalent:
- (a) Aut_𝔖(P) = 1.
- (b) The group scheme Aut_{X/k}(P) of connection-preserving automorphisms has dimension 0. It embeds in PGL_2,k by restriction to a fibre, so it is the centralizer of the monodromy.
- (c) P is of neither of two types:
  - (α) induced from a G_m-𝔖-bundle, i.e. a line bundle L with connection; then P = P(L ⊕ O), the projective closure of V(L).
  - (β) induced from a G_a-𝔖-bundle, i.e. an 𝔖-extension 0 → O_X → E → O_X → 0 (trivial structures on the O_X's); then P = P(E), the projective closure of the corresponding G_a-torsor.

A margin note says the intersection of the two types is the trivial 𝔖-structures.

Where this leads (next page). G = PGL_2 with Lie algebra 𝔤, self-dual via the Killing form.
- Poincaré duality gives H^0_DR(ad P) ≅ H^2_DR(ad P)^∨.
- The Euler characteristic is χ = 3(2−2g).
- Hence dim H^1 = 2·dim Aut + 6g − 6. Here H^0 = Lie Aut and H^1 is the tangent space to M_g^𝔖.
- So the trivial-Aut locus is formally smooth over M_g of relative dimension 6g−6 and plausibly rigid. Relative representability is expected, in Artin algebraic spaces.

This page is the definitional and non-degeneracy step of that deformation-theoretic analysis.
errors: (b) does not imply (a) for PGL_2. A connection-preserving automorphism group of dimension 0 need not be trivial. Irreducible monodromy with image in the normalizer of a torus (dihedral case) has centralizer containing Z/2. Image the Klein four-group V_4 ⊂ PGL_2 has centralizer V_4. So only (a) ⇒ (b) ⟺ (c) holds. The same issue undermines the next page's claim that the condition gives 'no finite automorphisms'.

Calling the condition 'P irréductible' is non-standard. Excluding only G_m- and G_a-reductions still allows connections that reduce to the Borel B but to neither G_m nor G_a (non-split, non-abelian monodromy in B). These are reducible but have trivial centralizer. Thus (b) ⟺ (c) is correct, in characteristic 0 at least, but the 'irreducible' gloss is not.

Minor: types α and β overlap in more than the trivial structure if one only asks for some reduction. For example, finite-order monodromy can be conjugated into G_m. The margin remark should be read as concerning reductions with trivial connection.

Dimension and representability statements implicitly assume characteristic 0. In characteristic p, 'connections' versus stratifications and the Killing-form self-duality of pgl_2 (fails for p = 2) need care.

ideas.what: Moduli over M_g of curves equipped with a flat PGL_2-bundle (P^1-bundle with integrable connection), defined using a rigidifying level structure on curves
ideas.modern_name: Relative de Rham moduli space M_dR(X/M_g, PGL_2); relative character variety over M_g
ideas.usually_credited_to: Simpson (Moduli of representations of the fundamental group I/II, 1994) for the relative de Rham moduli; Goldman, Hitchin and others for the analytic picture
ideas.where_published: Rigidifying functors and level structures appear in Grothendieck's Séminaire Cartan exposés (1960-61); the de Rham moduli itself does not, as far as I know.

ideas.what: Criterion: connection-preserving automorphisms are finite iff the bundle does not reduce, compatibly with the connection, to G_m (P(L⊕O), L flat) or to G_a (P(E), E a flat extension of O by O)
ideas.modern_name: Centralizer of monodromy finite iff representation is not reducible to a torus or unipotent subgroup ('good'/'regular' points of character varieties)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in character variety theory (Goldman 1984; Johnson–Millson 1987)

ideas.what: Use of these conditions to control deformations: H^0_DR(ad) = Lie Aut, duality H^0 ≅ (H^2)^∨, χ = 3(2−2g), giving relative dimension 6g−6 (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Deformation theory of flat G-bundles; dimension (2g−2)·dim G of the character variety

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, in characteristic-free scheme language with a rigidification of M_g, the relative moduli of curves with flat PGL_2-bundles as the ambient space for projective structures and uniformization, ahead of its later formal treatment by Simpson. This is a historical-priority detail (undated), not a new mathematical result.
missed.quote: Considérons $M_g^{\mathfrak{S}}(S)$ = courbes algébriques relatives $X$ de genre $g$ sur $S$, munies d'un fibré par droites projectives $P$ sur $X$, avec une $\mathfrak{S}$-structure
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's direct engagement with what became the relative de Rham / non-abelian Hodge moduli over M_g, linking it to his uniformization program. Of historical interest only.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard setup: moduli of curves with flat PGL_2-bundles, the non-degeneracy criterion via G_m/G_a reductions, and deformation theory, all now well known (Goldman, Simpson). The equivalence (a)⟺(b) is actually false because of dihedral and Klein-four monodromy. Historically interesting as Grothendieck's own formulation, but no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'foncteur rigidifiant (p. ex. de Torelli[?] d'idéaux convenables[?])' is more plausibly 'p. ex. de Jacobi d'échelon convenable', i.e. level-n Jacobi structures, Grothendieck's standard rigidification. Uncertain.
'un point la clôture projective de V(L)' should read 'on prend la clôture projective de V(L)', matching the parallel '(on prend P(E))' in β.
'GP(1)' is Grothendieck's notation for PGL(1) of P^1, i.e. PGL_2; '$G_{m,0}$' is likely just 'G_m'.
'(connexion[?] lisse[?])' is plausibly '(connexion intégrable)' or a stratification gloss for the 𝔖-structure.
'telle que ∀ s pt. géométrique de S, P_s sur X_s ne provienne pas ... de façon structurale ni d'un G_m ⊂ GP(1), ni d'un G_a ⊂ GP(1)': 'à un' should be read 'd'un' (reduction of structure group).
The left-margin note reads roughly 'l'intersection des deux types est les 𝔖-structures triviales (i.e. ... triviales)'.
